summary: Off-registry HTTPS tarball dependency enables install-time code delivery
details: The package ships an inert index.js stub but declares its sole dependency `ltidisafe` as a direct HTTPS tarball URL (https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-3.8.8.tgz) in package.json rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches and installs whatever bytes that URL returns, including any lifecycle scripts contained in the fetched tarball, bypassing npm registry version pinning and integrity controls. The scoped package name under @fcsmc with no README, no description, and an empty main is consistent with a dependency-confusion lure whose only on-install effect is to resolve attacker-controlled code from a third-party storage bucket.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
